title: Inputs and Outputs
summary: How a parent component passes data down and a child sends events back up.
heading: Inputs and Outputs

blocks.text: Apps are trees of components, so neighbours need to share. The rule is one-directional and simple: a parent passes data down to a child through an input, and a child sends events up to its parent through an output. Data down, events up.

blocks.caption: Data flows down through inputs; events flow up through outputs.
blocks.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 440 150' role='img' aria-label='Parent passes input down to child, child emits output up to parent'><defs><marker id='io-ar' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='6' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z' fill='currentColor'/></marker></defs><g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='150' y='12' width='140' height='44' rx='8'/><rect x='150' y='96' width='140' height='44' rx='8'/><line x1='195' y1='56' x2='195' y2='94' marker-end='url(#io-ar)'/><line x1='245' y1='94' x2='245' y2='58' marker-end='url(#io-ar)'/></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='13' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'><text x='220' y='39'>Parent</text><text x='220' y='123'>Child</text></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' opacity='0.75' font-family='monospace'><text x='150' y='79'>input ↓</text><text x='300' y='79'>output ↑</text></g></svg>

blocks.text: Keeping data flowing one way (down) and events flowing the other (up) is what makes big component trees predictable — you always know who owns the data.

sections.title: Example 1: passing data down with input()

blocks.text: An input() is how a child receives a value. It returns a signal, so you read it by calling it with () — and the view updates automatically if the parent changes it. You can give it a default value.

blocks.label: greeting.ts (child)

blocks.text: The parent sets it with property binding — the same [ ] from Chapter 20. A plain string needs no brackets; use brackets to bind to a value.

blocks.label: app.html (parent)
blocks.code:
<app-greeting name="Asha" />        <!-- static text -->
<app-greeting [name]="userName" />  <!-- bound to a property -->

blocks.caption: The parent's value lands in the child's input signal.
blocks.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 440 120' role='img' aria-label='Parent userName flows into the child name input'><defs><marker id='in-ar' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='6' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z' fill='currentColor'/></marker></defs><g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='15' y='40' width='170' height='44' rx='8'/><rect x='255' y='40' width='170' height='44' rx='8'/><line x1='185' y1='62' x2='253' y2='62' marker-end='url(#in-ar)'/></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' font-family='monospace'><text x='100' y='66'>userName = 'Asha'</text><text x='340' y='60'>name()</text><text x='340' y='76' font-size='10' opacity='0.7'>input</text></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='10' text-anchor='middle' opacity='0.75' font-family='monospace'><text x='219' y='52'>[name]</text></g></svg>

blocks.text: Inputs can do more than hold a default. These options come up constantly in real components.

blocks.label: input options

blocks.text: input.required is great for values a component can't work without — you get a clear error instead of a silent bug.

sections.title: Example 2: sending events up with output()

blocks.text: An output() lets a child notify its parent. The child calls .emit(value); the value it sends becomes $event in the parent. Type the output so the payload is checked.

blocks.label: like-button.ts (child)
app.ts (parent)

blocks.caption: The child emits a value; it arrives as $event in the parent.
blocks.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 440 120' role='img' aria-label='Child emits liked event up to the parent handler'><defs><marker id='out-ar' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='6' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L6,3 L0,6 Z' fill='currentColor'/></marker></defs><g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='255' y='40' width='170' height='44' rx='8'/><rect x='15' y='40' width='170' height='44' rx='8'/><line x1='253' y1='62' x2='187' y2='62' marker-end='url(#out-ar)'/></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' font-family='monospace'><text x='100' y='60'>onLike($event)</text><text x='100' y='76' font-size='10' opacity='0.7'>parent</text><text x='340' y='66'>liked.emit(1)</text></g><g fill='currentColor' font-size='10' text-anchor='middle' opacity='0.75' font-family='monospace'><text x='219' y='52'>(liked)</text></g></svg>

blocks.text: Most real components use both. Here a stepper receives its current count as an input and emits the new count whenever a button is pressed — the parent stays the owner of the value.

blocks.label: stepper.ts (child)

blocks.text: Because the input is count and the output is countChange, the parent can shorten those two lines to a two-way binding: [(count)]="total" — that's the next chapter.

sections.title: Example 4: passing an object as input

blocks.text: Inputs aren't limited to strings — they carry any type: numbers, booleans, arrays, or whole objects. A card component can take a full user object.

blocks.label: user-card.ts (child)

blocks.text: Brackets are required here — [user] binds to a real object. Without brackets the child would receive the literal string "currentUser".

sections.title: Example 5: a list item that emits its id

blocks.text: A very common pattern: render a list of child components, and let each one tell the parent when it's clicked or removed. The child emits its own id; the parent owns the list and removes it.

blocks.label: todo-item.ts (child)
app.ts (parent)

blocks.text: The parent keeps ownership of the list; the child just announces "remove me" by id. That's data down, events up in action.

items: An input is a signal — read it with name(); give it a default.
Set an input from the parent with [name]="value".
A child fires an output with thing.emit(payload); the parent reads $event.
An input x plus output xChange can be used as two-way [(x)].
